events.text: Chase the Dark

An abandoned barge washes up in Skullport on the River Sargauth and is impounded by the Skullport Island Registry. They aution off the most unusual piece of cargo, a white dragon egg, to the owners of Hired Horrors. Concerns arise in the town that the mysterious egg's parents might come looking for it.

Knight-Commanders Ian Graham and Carolyn Skyhawk are struck down by the Consortium of the Bloody Fang, acting through the magically coerced Carston Willow, who cast a lightning bolt at them as they were leaving a grand post-war ball being held at Griffon Hall. Knights and knight-squires rush the two off to the Halls of Morning Light, where attending Lathanderites manage to revive Carolyn Skyhawk, but are unable to save Ian Graham.
Nouméa Drathchuld relinquishes her role as Magister in favor of becoming one of Mystra's Chosen. Azuth offers the position to Talatha Vaerovree.

After more than a decade of isolation from her followers, the goddess Waukeen is freed from her prison by a band of adventurers and resumes her place in the heavens. This date becomes another of the many holy days for the church of Waukeen.
War erupts in southern Amn as Sythillis and his armies ally with the church of Cyric, seeking Maztican gold.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 154

events.text: War erupts in the Silver Marches as Obould Many-Arrows and his army of orcs, goblins, and frost giants Shallows attack Mithral Hall.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 150

events.text: The Battle of Shallows: the village of Shallows is destroyed by the Many-Arrows horde.
At the same time, Proffit and his army of trolls attack, conquer, and destroy Nesmé.
Mintar and the Church of Bane conquer the Tethyrian town of Kzelter.
Three statues created from living beings transmuted by Vendes Baenre revert to living form, attacking their Gracklstugh owners before dissolving into water.
cites: Drizzt Do'Urden's Guide to the Underdark, с. 61

events.text: The navy of Ravens Bluff is destroyed in a surprise pirate attack. That same night, the city is attacked by a monstrous mercenary army led by Myrkyssa Jelan. Traitors in the government and the abduction of the Lord Mayor ensure chaos reigns for six months. If not for the large number of adventurers in the city at the time, Raven's Bluff would surely have fallen.
cites: The City of Ravens Bluff, с. 5

events.text: Sea zombies and the ghosts of pirates attack Telflamm but are turned back by the Church of Tempus.
The Royal Navy of the Moonshae Isles sinks twenty Nelanther pirate ships in Firedrake Bay at the cost of only six of their own vessels.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 30

events.text: A plague strikes Waterdeep's Dock Ward, but is quickly contained by the city's priests. A secretive group of werecats known as the Eyes of the Evening determine that the outbreak was caused by a cult of Talona-worshiping wererats.
Mirtul 3–11: Fzoul Chembryl summons the Tyrantfog, slaying many Cyricists across the Heartlands and empowering Iyachtu Xvim with the power of many Banite relics and holy sites.

Tiamat begins channeling some of her divine power through the sphere of annihilation known as Entropy, already worshiped in Luthcheq. The cultists begin receiving divine spells from her and smaller spheres break off from the larger one, which the cultists can control. Tiamat also grants the cultists the service of some of her abishai.

Lolth's avatar steps through a portal deep in Undermountain to reclaim her long-lost Flame Sword hidden there by Halaster Blackcloak. The lone adventurer known only as the Khelbenite defeats the avatar with the artifact being destroyed in the ensuing explosion of divine energy.
Duggan McKnuckles, Bokkum, and Stokkum are killed in an attack on their caravan by orcs and frost giants near the Spine of the World, on their way to Shallows.
The Lord of Zhentil Keep, Orgauth, is slain by the fallen paladin Scyllua Darkhope as the final step to her becoming a blackguard mere months after Orgauth himself caused her to fall from grace.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 164

events.text: Dagna Waybeard, dwarven general from Mithral Hall, is killed by trolls when he tries to protect refugees from destroyed Nesmé.
Dagnabbit, the son of dwarven general Dagna Waybeard, the lead military commander of Mithral Hall's armed forces, dies during the Battle of Shallows.
The insane priest of Kelemvor, Vraer of Scornubel, dies challenging the White Fate colony of beholders for their territory southeast of Llorkh.
Asborn Moonstar ventures into the Undermountain in search of a crystal rose and perishes in the pursuit.
Undead necromancer Ghoulmaster sends resurrected members of the Cassalanter to attack citizens of Waterdeep before being slain by the Khelbenite.
Horazak, the devil-blooded orc slaver is slain in his Undermountain fortress.
The Shaking Plague strikes Scardale, destroying much of the Sembian garrison.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 136–137

events.text: Large numbers of fey, of many varieties, migrate from Faerie to Myrloch Vale and Winterglen Forest on Gwynneth.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 30

events.text: The Church of Dugmaren establishes a temple called the Athenaeum of Philosophy in Silverymoon to ensure a dwarven contribution to the collected knowledge of the new nation of Luruar.
The Tower of Swift Death, a temple of Bhaal just outside Tyraturos in Thay, officially switches to the worship of Cyric, twelve years after the death of their god.
The Emerald Enclave seizes control of the Whamite Isles.

The Shadow Thieves under the leadership of Grandmaster Xabash return to Waterdeep and ally with the drow forces of Matron Azurna to bring down the City of Splendors. The same year the Shadow Thieves' were driven out from their stronghold in Undermountain.

Clangeddin's Hearth attempts to take over their (Clan Melairkyn) ancestral ground in the Undermountain only to be slaughtered by Matron Azurna's drown and their corpses reanimated as lich's Morik Stormhand's playthings.
Khelben "Blackstaff" Arunsun is put on trial in Berdusk by the High Harpers and found guilty. He retreats to Waterdeep and forms the Moonstars.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 150

events.text: Queen Zaranda and King Haedrak III of Tethyr have triplets: Sybille, Coram, and Rhindaun.
Eskylla, one of the drow priestesses of Matron Azurna, abandoned her faith in favor of worshiping Eilistraee, and joins Sabrae Tellendon's temple.

The Guildmaster of the Shadow Thieves in Waterdeep, Georges, leaves the guild in order to commit his life to his lover Meryth Phaulkon, helping the dissolving of the guild's operations in Undermountain.
The wedding of Devana Melshimber and Rivven Melshimber takes place with the bride's sister, Tryola Perrentine captured and enslaved by Horazak.
Riatavin and Trailstone secede from Amn to Tethyr.

Ninety percent of the population of the Untheric city of Shussel vanish overnight in "the Vanishing". The city is taken by Mulhorandi military forces who use its port as a supply and troop route in their war against Unther.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 187

Respectable citizens of Waterdeep become designed by a small army of spectators who were assigned to "guard" powerful magical items, such as Piergeiron the Paladinson's sword and Khelben Arunsun's staff. The swarm is sent by Halaster Blackcloak's apprentice Ibbalar Thrul.
The Black Wand of Myrkul recovered from the dead god's abandoned temple in the Underdark and entrusted to Khelben Arunsun to be destroyed.

events.text: An attempt is made on the life of Arklem Greeth by two members of the Arcane Brotherhood. Arklem survives but the old mage is badly injured and has to flee Luskan. He travels in secret to Mirabar, where he meets Nyphithys, an erinyes who helps him to become a lich. Revitalized in undeath, Arklem returns to the Host Tower with a force of summoned devils and violently reclaims his place as Archmage Arcane. He then sets about rebuilding his broken organization and bringing the High Captains under his sway again, after they had become more independent over the last few years.
Halarim Threesilver writes home to his family that he has located one of only two known copies of the third volume of A Harper's Companion. He is never heard from again.
"Waylaid"
Galaeron Nihmedu unwittingly releases the phaerimm from their prison under the dunes of Anauroch, the phaerimm quickly isolate and besiege Evereska.
Khelben "Blackstaff" Arunsun along with several other Chosen of Mystra muster a relief army in Waterdeep and set out to lift the phaerimm siege on Evereska.
Galaeron Nihmedu and Melegaunt Tanthul, a prince of Shade travel to Karse where they recover the Karsestone, destroying the lich Wulgreth who had used the stone as his phylactery.

Nalavarauthatoryl leads an army of goblins and other monsters, despoiling much of Cormyr. The elf-dragon and King Azoun IV slay each other in battle. This conflict is often referred to as the Goblin War.
Drow of Clan Auzkovyn battle with priests of Tempus at the Abbey of the Sword, after coming through an unguarded portal deep beneath the re-built castle.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 121

events.text: Renegade sun elves, human sea-wolves, and drow join together to attack the island of Evermeet. A powerful spell destroys the Tower of the Sun and one third of the island's mages are killed.

events.text: Nightal 28 to Nightal 30: The Battle of Rocnest, the first major battle in the siege of Evereska.

The Righteous Man, guildmaster of the Night Knives thieves' guild of Selgaunt and a powerful priest of Mask, summons Yrsillar, a mighty greater dread, to his temple beneath the guild headquarters. Drasek Riven, one of his lieutenants and a secret member of the Zhentarim, frees the demon by disrupting the protective circle containing it.
A lesser dread and a number of ghouls attack Stormweather Towers in Selgaunt, slaying over twenty guests and house guards. Thazienne Uskevren is left gravely wounded.
With the help of Jak Fleet, Erevis Cale infiltrates the Night Knives former headquarters and confronts Yrsillar.

Eleasis 27: Alyn Telarson writes a large report to Khelben Arunsun on Serôs, giving a non-exhaustive overview of the undersea realm in relation to the various islands and coastal areas on the surface.
Alustriel Silverhand assumes the title of "High Lady of the Silver Marches" and forms the League of the Silver Marches, officially turning the confederacy of Luruar into a new country.
cites: The North: Guide to the Savage Frontier: Cities & Civilization, с. 55–56

events.text: The Northlander kings swear fealty to High Queen Alicia Kendrick, giving birth to a new nation titled the United Moonshae Isles.
The zulkirs of Thay, tired of incessant battles with Aglarond, offer a truce. The Simbul accepts with reservations.
Orc warlord King Obould Many-Arrows established the Kingdom of Dark Arrows, laying claim to the mountains west of the Moonwood and north of the Evermoors.

Chieftain Grguch of Clan Karuck, a rogue chieftain of Obould's horde attacks both the Moonwood and Mithral Hall's new eastern wall. The attack on Moonwood most likely takes place in spring, after the thaw but before Wulfgar's return to Icewind Dale.

Violence becomes more and more common between the citizens of the United Moonshaes and the recent fey migrants to the Myrloch Vale. A verdant prince is said to be organizing the fey on the isle. Men sent by High Queen Alicia are either turned away by the fey, or go missing.

events.text: The autumn of 1372 DR in Tethyr marked the beginning and the end of the Bloody Fall. A short conflict between an ogre mage warlord Sythillis and the kingdom of Tethyr. The war's conclusion was the battle of Suldanessellar in which an unnamed hero battled the warlord and emerged victorious. The short but bloody conflict took several thousand lives and was later recorded in the Crimson Tides of Tethyr book of historic accounts.
Innovindil of the Moonwood and her pegasus steed Sunset are both killed in a skirmish with Clan Karuck on the western edge of her home.
Grguch of Clan Karuck, legendary among the orcs of the north, falls in battle with Bruenor Battlehammer, but the killing blow is from Obould.
Belshazu is slain in the Abyss by the drow wizard Pharaun Mizzrym.
Aribeth de Tylmarande was executed by Nasher Alagondar following her betrayal of Neverwinter.

On Midwinter night, the god Bane returns to Faerûn, bursting forth from the skin of his son, Iyachtu Xvim. With his divinity restored, Bane quickly gains the portfolio of fear, restoring him to a Greater Power.
The Shadovar melt large portions of the High Ice, causing widespread changes to Faerûn's climate and weather, leaving Western Faerûn beset by drought.
A volcano near the Citadel of Black Ash erupts, burying the citadel and killing all the followers of Gilgeam living there.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

events.text: The Purple Staves ally with the Nobanionites of Gulthmere Forest when they realize that they have nothing to fear from the group's settlement of the area. Later in the year, the first three fortified hamlets are completed at the edge of the forest.
Adventurers rescue Velvred Twohands, the five-year-old son of High Lord Kalahar Twohands of Loudwater, from agents of those who wish to kill his father.
The Guardians of the Weave are founded by the Waterdhavian wizard Aluvauna Thornym to combat the uptake of the Shadow Weave by magic-users.
The Dungeon of the Hark is cleared by the Red Fellowship (Loudwater), an army out of Loudwater.

Elminster Aumar clashes with the Shadovar, opening a rift to Avernus in the process. By expending his considerable magical repertoire Elminster closes the rift, only to be taken captive by the ex-archdevil Nergal.
Otar, a young orc chieftain from the High Forest becomes the new Green Regent, much to the outrage of many influential citizens of Loudwater.

events.text: Using a magical globe stolen from the study of the late Lord Thamalon Uskevren, the Cyricist shadow adept Vraggen locates the time and location where the Fane of Shadows will next appear on Toril.

Agents of Vraggen kill Sephris Dwendon, Chosen of Oghma, to stop him from helping Erevis Cale, Jak Fleet, and Drasek Riven from using the recovered globe to uncover the location of the Fane of Shadows. Undeterred, Erevis speaks with the man's spirit, who tells them the Fane will appear in the Moonmere, in Gulthmere Forest.

Arriving at the newly arrived Fane of Shadows, Erevis, Jak, and Drasek are too late to stop Vraggen. The Cyricist nearly succeeds in using the altar within the temple to transform into a shade, but is killed by the slaad Azriim, whom he thought was a half-drow ally. Stealing a sapling Weave Tap from the temple, Azriim and his allies escape. Erevis is nearly slain trying to save Jak, but saves himself by using the altar to turn himself into a shade.

Having survived the disappearance of the Fane of Shadows by being transported to the Plane of Shadow, Erevis and his companions eventually return to Toril only to discover that Vhostym's slaadi are planning to use a seed from the Weave Tap to siphon power from the mantle protecting Skullport. They arrive too late, and Skullport is nearly destroyed.

Eltab returns from hiding and attempts to wrest control of the land of Thay from Szass Tam but is apparently defeated by Thazienne Uskevren in a titanic battle. In reality, ancient bindings by the demonbinders of Narfell transported Eltab to the Citadel of Conjurers in Impiltur where he begins plotting his revenge anew.

Tower Reilloch on Evermeet is invaded by Daemonfey. Part of the Gatekeeper's Crystal is stolen.
Sarya Dlardrageth uses the Gatekeeper's Crystal to dispel the magical protection on Nar Kerymhoarth and gains access, freeing nearly two-thousand fey'ri.
Daelegoth Orndeir leads elite members of his Brotherhood of the Glorious Sun against an encampment of shadovar exploring the ruins of Karse. Brennus Tanthul is badly wounded and forced to flee.
An orc warband accompanied by daemonfey launch an overnight attack on Rheitheillathor in the High Forest. Although the wood elf inhabitants fought back, they were forced into retreat.
Seiveril Miritar resigns from Evermeet's ruling council.
The Battle of the Cwm sees the elves of Evereska and Evermeet victorious against the daemonfey armies, but not without heavy casualties.

The army from Everlund led by Methrammar Aerasumé is ambushed in the High Forest by the daemonfey and accompanying orcs. The daemonfey and orcs are driven back, but only one fey'ri is killed in exchange for a larger number of casualties on the other side.
Hillsfar breaks its alliance with House Dlardrageth. In response, the fey'ri attack the Red Plumes and destroy the First Lord's Tower, forcing Maalthiir into hiding.
The crusading army of Evermeet combined with the forces of Sembia and the Dalelands defeat the fey'ri legion and retake the city of Myth Drannor in the name of the elves.
The Battle of Selgaunt is fought. The forces of Selgaunt repel the attackers.

The rift was the result of the Shadowstorm, brought forth by the Sharran priestess Elyril Hraven using a ritual found in The Leaves of One Night.

The whole continent of Faerûn is beset by an unusual year-long rain of meteors and lightning storms. In a series of visions, Bahamut and Tiamat instruct their followers to seek out the impact points of the meteors, as each contains some form of dragon egg. Although Bahamut's followers have the help of the Sisterhood of Essembra to recover the eggs that land on the Dalelands, members of the Church of Tiamat are more effective in retrieving most of the eggs. They bring back more than half to the Altar of Scales in Unthalass, in preparation for a possible new battle of the Dragonfall War. The rest of the eggs are recovered by Bahamut's followers, hatch on their own, or are lost.

Hostilities between all three soon resume along their shared borders and dragon raids cause chaos in the center of each country.

events.text: Amn's attempts to colonize Chult start to pay off their investment of money, ships, and people. The Amnians kidnap a whole tribe of so-called savage humanoid creatures from the deep jungles and relocate them to a caged preserve in the city of Athkatla.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Shalis Ptolexis, mother of the powerful mage Myrin Darkdance.
Ghaunadaur leaves the Demonweb Pits and moves his divine realm to the Deep Caverns after a failed assassination attempt by Lolth.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: A parasitic disease sweeps through Athkatla in Amn and kills one of the Council of Six. Citizens blame the tribe of Chultan humanoids being kept in a caged preserve in the city. An attempt is made to exterminate them but they escape into Amn's interior.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: An Elven High Magic ritual is preformed by drow wizards from the city of Sshamath, meant to convert members of the drow race untainted with the balor blood of Wendonai, including the followers of Eilistraee, back into dark elves. However, the ritual (which saw Eilistraee's intervention) only affects hundreds among the few thousand followers of the Dark Maiden (which she has as a lesser goddess). Among the faithful of Eilistraee, the souls of the newly transformed dark elves are allowed to enter Arvandor by Corellon Larethian (even though Eilistraee's realm, which continues to exist, is already in Arvandor, and the souls of her followers within it are drow or dark elves).

Myrmeen Lhal petitions Regent Alusair Obarskyr of Cormyr to find a replacement for her as Lord of Arabel. Before being given leave to retire her post, she begins moving to Suzail, leaving the city in the hands of her herald.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 3

cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159

events.text: Ascendancy of the Last ends.
A canal that links the Lake of Steam to the Nagaflow river is completed, linking the Sea of Fallen Stars and the western oceans.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: The village of Galardoun near Scornubel is abandoned after a wasting disease kills most inhabitants.
cites: Dungeon 196: Eye on the Realms: The Ghost Knight of Galardoun

events.text: Araevin Teshurr successfully restores Myth Drannor's mythal. He tours the continent, visiting Waterdeep, Aglarond and Sildëyuir. He then sets out to find Auseriel where he meets and befriends Prince Lamruil. The two set out to find the missing Maura Silverhand.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Sembia comes entirely under the rule of the Twelve Princes of Shade and begins its transformation into a state of Netheril.
Zhentarim Hatemaster, Cvaal Daoran, dissolves Phlan's Council of Ten, establishing himself as its Lord Protector.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 52

events.text: This year is known as the Year of the Dull Blade in the Black Chronology.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 157

events.text: Final Gate ends.
Northern Faerûn is hit by a freak cold snap that ruins food crops and animal forage. Urban centers all over the continent see much of their populace go hungry.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: The food shortage exacerbates the Shou emigration out of the Unapproachable East.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: This year is known as the Year of the Fool in the Black Chronology.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 157

events.text: Starmantle and Westgate seek to advertise themselves as the destination of choice for Shou immigrants.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: This year is known as the Year of Unwelcome Guests in the Black Chronology.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 157

events.text: The War of Gold and Gloom comes to an end when the Army of Gold discovers the long-forgotten history of Clan Duergar, which precipitates an attack from an army of illithid thralls. The duergar and gold dwarf armies join with each other to repel the army and the duergar take the most casualties. The Army of Gold offers an alliance to what remains of the Army of Steel and the united dwarves march to retake Shanatar where they hope to be better prepared to repel the inevitable second attack from Oryndoll.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: The Shadowbane War occurs when Netheril attacks the Zhentarim. Zhentil Keep and the Citadel of the Raven are destroyed, and the Zhentarim's power over the Moonsea is broken.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 65

events.text: Cvaal Daoran of Phlan single-handedly slays a Prince of Shade during the Shadowbane War.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 65

events.text: Triel Baenre is murdered by her sister Quenthel.

The Morndinsamman openly attack Laduguer and Deep Duerra. Laduguer is killed by Moradin and Deep Duerra is killed by Clangeddin but Gorm Gulthyn and Haela Brightaxe also die in the battle. Without the support of Laduguer and Deep Duerra, the plane of Hammergrim disperses into the Astral Plane.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Fzoul Chembryl is slain during the Netherese siege of Zhentil Keep and is elevated as an exarch by Bane.
The ulitharid Galgast takes command of and revitalizes the Sept of Ill'Ghact. Plans begin to proceed apace with the stalled goal of restoring the city of Phanlinksal.

House Horlbar and House Kenafin, both accused of heresy, join forces, creating House Melarn. Named after Lolth's Lady Penitent, they (and many refugees from Ched Nasad) strive to prove themselves devout by intruding into the personal business of minor houses and exposing any perceived heresies to the public.
The Zhentarim breaks away from the influence of the Church of Bane following the death of Fzoul Chembryl, and the Church of Cyric attempts to fill the void.
Lord Protector Cvaal Daoran of Phlan forms a pact with the dark fey of the Quivering Forest, gaining protection for Phlan in exchange for a promise to prohibit logging and travel in the forest.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 81

events.text: The Durpari city of Vaelan becomes renowned across Faerûn for its exotic body art which utilizes living crystal that also improves the talents of the subject.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: This year is known as the Year of Unjust Rewards in the Black Chronology.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 157

events.text: In a misunderstanding and resultant quarrel over Tymora, Helm is slain by Tyr. Tymora herself moves her divine realm to the House of the Triad. The gods suspect Cyric but can't prove anything.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Ilmater and Siamorphe move their divine realms to Brightwater at Sune's invitation.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Azoun V is crowned king of Cormyr. His first major act as king is to attempt to set up a jury system in Cormyrian law courts. He faces stiff opposition from the nobles as it would mean that any legal accusations they make against commoners would not automatically be settled in their favour. He eventually relents under the political pressure, but vows that one day he will successfully enact his decree.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Now that her time as Steel Regent is ended, the king's aunt Alusair is made Marshal of Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: Gedrin Shadowbane, a young rogue living in Westgate, had a vision in which Helm was slain by Tyr and Helm's godhood flowed into Tyr, restoring his sight. Later, Gedrin had a second vision in which Tyr was slain by Orcus and Tyr's godhood merged with Torm's. After the visions, Gedrin formulated the Heresy of the Threefold God and formed the Eye of Justice and drove the Night Masks from Westgate.
This year is known as the Year of Stolen Thrones in the Black Chronology.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159

cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: The armies of Szass Tam assault the Keep of Sorrows.
Cyric, aided and abetted by Shar, murders Mystra. With her death, the Weave convulses and blue flames envelop the realms and surrounding planes.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: An army made up of undead and creatures from the Shadowfell belonging to the Ghost King assault the Spirit Soaring and Carradoon in Erlkazar.
Native Dambrathans revolt and drive their half-drow masters from the land.
Asmodeus fuses with the dying Azuth, who fell into the Nine Hells, saving the God of Wizards' life but stealing his divine powers, and thus the archdevil becomes a god.
cites: Ashes of the Tyrant: Hardcover, с. 398–399

events.text: Deneir writes himself into the Weave via the Metatext in an attempt to stabilize it.
Lathander, Tyr and Sune imprison Cyric in the Supreme Throne for 1000 years.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Lathander reveals himself to be Amaunator in the weeks just after the Spellplague.
Priests of Hanali Celanil open a portal to Arvandor near Evereska, and learn that their deity exists in Arvandor only as an avatar of Sune.
Nobanion tried to save a pride of lions in Gulthandor from oncoming blue fire. He came in contact with the blue fire, and it mutated him into a dark and bestial lion with a mane of blue flame.
Cadderly Bonaduce sacrifices himself to keep the Ghost King in the Shadowfell.
Catti-brie dies, never recovering from being trapped between the Shadowfell and the Prime Material Plane after being caught in the blue fire of the collapsing Weave.
Regis dies the same night as Catti-brie, having become similarly trapped after trying to revive Catti-brie with the ruby pendant.
Imbrar II, king of Impiltur, dies without an heir, thus ending the Heltharn dynasty, and the monarchy in Impiltur.
Nasher Alagondar, king of Neverwinter, dies.
All of House Xorlarrin's miners in the Lustrum mine are killed by gemstone golems.
The dragon-king Tchazzar disappears in Threskel during the spellplague.
A young human wizard named Myrin becomes trapped by a pocket of spellplague and is transported to Waterdeep where she appears as a young woman trapped in blue flame.

Kepeshkmolik Thymara, guided by the goddess Selûne, reconstructs Djerad Thymar above the God-Tomb of the death Untherite god Nanna-Sin. The dragonborn spend the rest of the year fighting the spellscarred horrors of the former lands of Unther while founding the nation of Tymanther.
cites: Ashes of the Tyrant: Hardcover, с. 291–294

events.text: Quenthel Baenre attempts to dissolve the Ruling Council of Menzoberranzan to declare herself queen but her plans are foiled by the Spellplague.
With the Abyss sent into the Elemental Chaos, the Blood War its stalled it by a hundred years.
cites: Fire in the Blood: Hardcover 2014, с. 94

events.text: With Mystra's death, The Weave unravels. Being an integral part of the world, chaos ensues. Magic breaks its bonds, causing widespread destruction and calamity. This phenomenon is known as the Spellplague.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: The Wards of Silverymoon were shattered.

The Spellplague affects the landscape, making the ground rumble and heave up and down like the surface of the sea. Curtains of blue flame swept the landscape, reshaping the land by cutting crevasses or lifting and sculpting the plain into hills and ridges. Shards of earth wrenched themselves free and became earthmotes.

Sespech, the Golden Plains and the Nagalands become the foci for the Spellplague for at least the next century. They become collectively known as the Plaguewrought Lands and the terrain, natural laws, and any life left inside the boundaries of the place are continually warped and changed.
Halruaa is destroyed by the outbreak of the Spellplague, in such a catastrophic way that the explosion was felt as far as Waterdeep.
Shar turns the Plane of Shadow into the Shadowfell and the people of Faerûn meet its denizens soon after.
The Spellplague pulled back the Feywild into Toril's proximity, reopening the paths between the two planes again.
With his new found godly power, Asmodeus took advantage of the planar instability to hurl the Abyss to the Elemental Chaos in a attempt to end the Blood War.

In Hulburg, a fourth of the city is destroyed as parts of Abeir transpose themselves into the city's harbor. The Arches, dozens of pale green stone columns soaring hundreds of feet in the air, erupt from the seabed in a single night, creating the best harbor on the north shore of the Moonsea. In addition, equally-tall columns of malachite known as the Spires erupted from the ridge marking the western edge of the town, in some cases bursting through the old foundations of the ancient ruins.
The continent of Maztica is sent to the world of Abeir.
Approximately one third of all Cormyrean War Wizards die, go mad, or disappear over the next year.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: The merchant prince Nathur Hethkantan leads an ill-fated expedition to the Glaur Barrens, in the world of Abeir, in hopes to uncover the remains of the primordial Nehuhsta. During his travels, he founds the town of Rimlost. When the Spellplague is unleashed in the world of Abeir, Nathur mutates into a powerful dracolich.
cites: Dragon 375: Gontal: Dominions of Nehu, с. 78

events.text: The Glaur Barrens are created when the fortress of Glaur is destroyed by the Spellplague while on the world of Abeir. The explosion transposes the continent of Laerakond to the world of Toril, while sending the continent of Maztica to the world of Abeir.
Djerad Thymar was separated from Skelkor, a land of Laerakond, and falls on Unther, creating the Black Ash Plain and sending Unther to the continent of Shyr in Abeir.

Halruaan wizards, having divined the death of Mystra and the destruction of the Weave, were able to use the energy of the blue fire to save most of their kingdom by shifting it into Abeir, displacing part of that world to the Plane of Shadow.
This year is known as the Year of the Revelation in the Black Chronology.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 159
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 157

A meeting of resistance members against Szass Tam's takeover of Thay is attacked by a group of skeletons and an ulgurstasta under the control of one of the lich's minions. cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Wide expanses of the Sea of Fallen Stars seabed collapse into the Underdark. The resulting water level is lower than previously. Waters of the Vilhon Reach empty out into the lowered sea, revealing several Jhaamdathan ruins..
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: The Arnrock volcano in the Lake of Steam erupts violently, wiping out the halfling settlement that had sprung up on its long dormant crater.
The land of Luiren is flooded and destroyed by rising seas, transforming it into the Gulf of Luiren.
Genasi displaced from the land of Shyr on Abeir immediately begin establishing their own kingdom on Toril.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Realms of the Dead
Pieces

The Emerald Enclave starts despatching agents into the new Vilhon Wilds in an attempt to fight back the Spellplague. Their initial mission is protecting the natural world, but it will become a futile struggle against unnatural forces.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: The Murann Spice War opposing the Ophal and Ulvax families of Athkatla causes so many casualties that the Council of Six has to intervene, resulting in a massive rise in power for the Ophals.
Fiirnel'ther Vandree of House Vandree of Menzoberranzan assassinates her mother, Troken'ther, in order to assume leadership of her House. Before the end of the year, she is on the ruling council.
Zhentarim forces operating in the Tunlands are hampered as they are attacked by bullywug tribes dwelling in the Farsea Marshes.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: As they have lost access to magic, a few of the War Wizards of Cormyr start cross-training in martial arts and swordsmanship with the Purple Dragons. When they regain the use of magic, they become the first swordmages.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: The Gundwynd Clan is rendered extinct in Waterdeep after entering the burial portal in their family tomb in the City of the Dead to bury three members, shortly after the Spellplague first struck the city. All who emerge are permanently transformed into trolls or giants.
A mysterious black monolith is sometimes sighted emerging from the sea off the Cormyrean coast, but always in different locations.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Filfaeril Selzair Obarskyr, the dowager Dragon Queen of Cormyr, dies.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Following Filfaeril's funeral, Alusair Obarskyr is seen arguing briefly with her nephew, King Azoun V, in private, before storming from the court. She is not seen again for years, though there are rumors her riding through Cormyr's frontiers.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Arilyn Moonblade begins training Azariah Craulnober at the behest of the latter's father, Elaith Craulnober.
cites: Realms of Infamy: The More Things Change

events.text: Realms of Infamy
"The More Things Change" ends.
Auril's Winter Hall assimilates the Winged Mother's floating palace into her domain.
Randal Morn, the legendary leader of Daggerdale dies.
Athror Baergil, brother of famous Captain Darrask Baergil of the Riders of Mistledale, dies, aged 90.
cites: Candlekeep forum: Questions for Ed Greenwood (2011): Captain Baergil

events.text: The elves of the militant Eldreth Veluuthra, seize control of the Hullack Forest to use it as a base for their anti-human operations.
The Eye of Justice drives Orbakh and the Night Masks from Westgate.
The druid circle in Cedarspoke is taken over by Zalaznar Crinios, a human turned treant. Firemane, a lesser druid who can turn into a lion, also becomes prominent.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Sathrin Cormaeril arrives in Daggerdale upon hearing of his uncle Randal Morn's death and claims the throne.

Seeking protection from the Spellplague, Pros and Ilipur, two cities on the Dragon Coast, petition to become vassal-states of Cormyr. Although King Azoun V accepts their plea, they are already doomed by the receding Sea of Fallen Stars.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: King Azoun V of Cormyr makes a formal objection to the Dales Council in Archendale over Sembian investors purchasing large tracts of land in the southern Dalelands. His emissary is rebuffed.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Many people with spellscars and those seeking to get one start traveling to the Plaguewrought Lands. The Order of Blue Fire welcomes them in Ormpetarr.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: The Emerald Enclave starts trying to half the flow of spellscarred pilgrims traveling through Turmish.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Cormyr tries to retake the Hullack Forest from the occupying Eldreth Veluuthra, ending when King Azoun V turns his attention to the more pressing threats from neighboring Netheril and Sembia.
Daerlun is finally annexed by Cormyr, owing to its mixed Cormyrean and Sembian heritage and Netherese rule.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Rault, who will one day be known as "Rault the Wise" and rule as Jarl of Norland, is born.
The Netherese enclave of Sakkors reappears above Daerlun in the night. In the morning, there is civil unrest across the city and King Azoun V of Cormyr dispatches elite swordmages to establish order.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: A great plague known variously as the Putrescent Anathema or the Plaguebringer's Blight brings devastation to Goldenfields and Waterdeep, primarily to the poor as the supply of grain plummets.

Most of the effects of the Spellplague end during this year, with only a few places, known as plaguelands, still afflicted by the wild magic brought by the cataclysm. Most arcane magic returns to a semblance of normality, with a handful of major changes to the way spells are cast.
cites: Dragon 362: Countdown to the Realms: Spellplague: The Wailing Years

events.text: Nogah finds the Dreamheart in a drowned illithid city deep under the Sea of Fallen Stars.
King Azoun V of Cormyr marries Nalara Marliir the daughter of Lord High Marshal Dauneth Marliir and Krystin Lhal.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 61

events.text: Nogah is stripped of her whip status when she started to preach about an ancient power revealed to her by the Dreamheart. When the kuo-toa of Olleth attempt to stop her, she summons the kraken Gethshemeth.
Nogah is killed by poisoned crossbow bolts fired by aberrant kuo-toa.

The ninth emperor Chin of Shou Lung decrees that hengeyokai and spirit folk of Sheng Ti province can take the civil service examination to join the mandarinate. This is done as recognition for the help of these non-humans in stabilizing the province after the influence of the Feywild ran rampant following the Spellplague.
cites: Dragon 404: Ecology of the Hengeyokai, с. 4

events.text: Tsarra Chaadren, the Blackstaff of Waterdeep, as well as her heir and many members of the Moonstars are killed by a coven of vampire wizards in the Stump Bog.

Caladnei, Royal Magician of Cormyr, is struck by the expanding effects of the Spellplague in a heavily warded spellcasting chamber in Castle Obarskyr and is killed. The Dragonskull Chamber, with its wards warped so that anyone with spellcasting ability can't approach without becoming violently ill, is ordered abandoned.

Despite the risk to her sanity, Kyriani Agrivar takes the Blackstaff back to Waterdeep. With Open Lord Caladorn Cassalanter at her side, Kyriani proclaims herself the new Blackstaff from on top of Blackstaff Tower, beginning a tradition.
War Hero Ishual Karanok merges the different coinages of the city-states of Chessenta into a single currency.
Wrath of the Blue Lady begins.
